To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a gut-mesh protein regulates Duox-mediated reactive oxygen species production, thereby contributing to maintaining homeostatic balance in the insect gut.
a Mesh-mediated MAPK signalling cascade regulates the expression of a Duox enzyme, which in turn contributes to maintaining gut homeostasis by controlling the proliferation of the gut microbiota.
a membrane-associated protein named Mesh regulates homeostasis of the insect gut by controlling Duox expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which insects regulate homeostasis in their gut microbiome.
the role of Mesh in maintaining homeostasis of the insect gut by regulating the expression of Duox, which is involved in the regulation of bacterial proliferation in the insect gut.
the mechanisms that hosts have evolved to maintain homeostasis in their guts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mesh is a novel regulator of the gut microbiota and that it does so by controlling the expression of Duox, which is a dual oxidase.
the Mesh-Duox signalling pathway is essential for maintaining gut homeostasis in Drosophila and Aedes aegpti, and that this pathway is activated by a blood meal in the latter species.
this study shows that the Mesh-mediated pathway is a central regulatory mechanism in the gut microbiota homeostasis of insects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insect gut maintains its homeostasis via a Mesh-Duox signalling pathway.
Mesh is a gut-membranes-associated protein that regulates Duox expression and thus contributes to homeostasis in insect gut.
the Mesh-Duox signalling pathway is an important homeostatic pathway that regulates gut microbiome in both Drosophila and mosquito.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Mesh-Duox signalling pathway is a conserved homeostatic mechanism in the insect gut, which regulates the quantity and composition of gut bacterial communities in both Aedes aeypti and D. melanogaster.
the Mesh-Duox signalling pathway is a key mechanism in the regulation of the gut microbiota in both Drosophila and mosquitoes.
the Mesh-mediated pathway regulates the expression of the Duox enzyme in the gut epithelium.
